# codex-0.171.0 verification

Status: Qualified anchor with bounded local-only store inspection.

Six compatibility cells passed on Codex 0.171.0 (homebrew cask
`/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/codex/0.171.0/bin/codex`) with gpt-6-astra on
2026-11-20; exec streaming remains the intentional skip ("not
token-granular"). The question probe passed. Synthetic turns and
later-process HERON-CODEX-1121 recall passed. Exec emits no compaction
signal. No native compaction failure was observed in the successful
qualifying run, and no failure outcome was forced. The npm source remains
@openai/codex (npm latest 0.171.0 at capture time).

## Probe settings

- Automatic compaction was exercised with `model_auto_compact_token_limit=20000`, a config override the probe set for its own turns. Lowered thresholds are a probe setting, not an HCN default.
- The executable under test is the machine's own homebrew codex install, already upgraded to 0.171.0 for this refresh; no harness was upgraded or reconfigured by the probe. `version-source.snapshot.json` records the install.
- The model catalog and the four app-server request schemas came from protocol metadata calls against the same executable: `model/list` with and without `includeHidden`, and `codex app-server generate-json-schema --experimental`. No turn was started, no model inference ran and no auth probe was made.
- The 0.171.0 roster adds `gpt-6.2-sol` and `gpt-6.2-astra` (visible and includeHidden; nothing dropped). Both carry the 6.x ladder `low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra` in `supportedReasoningEfforts`; `ultra` stays outside hcn's closed effort vocabulary.
- The four request schemas: `ThreadStartParams` is byte-identical to the 0.165.0 and 0.169.0 snapshots; the other three differ from 0.165.0's minor definition changes but are byte-identical to the (unmerged) 0.169.0 captures.
- The `project_doc_max_bytes` error item on turn 1 (combined user instructions above 32768 bytes) is pre-existing native behavior, present in the 0.169.0 captures too; its size reflects the operator's global instruction file, and no content is echoed.

## Replacement installation and store-observation limits

The rollout holds 2 `item_completed/ContextCompaction` events (lines 31 and 55) and 2 `compacted` rows with nonempty `replacement_history` arrays (8 and 9 items), window numbers 1 and 2, window links and `latest_token_usage_record` present. The payload-nested `compacted` row schema is unchanged from 0.165.0/0.169.0.

The store read was bounded and structural, over this probe's own synthetic rollout only, resolved through the repository's own store resolver. Large rows were truncated: the complete replacement contents were not inspected. Only derived structural metadata is included, not raw protected stores or encrypted content.

Lowered thresholds do not establish full-capacity handling or lossless recall. A smoke pass alone does not prove native replacement-history installation.

## What this anchor does not establish

- Native model acceptance was not re-probed per model on 0.171.0; the model catalog is the native roster, and the effort ladders come from the catalog's own `supportedReasoningEfforts`.
- No native compaction failure was observed and none was forced.

## Captured evidence

`seven.snapshot.json` and `questions.snapshot.json` are the smoke-suite receipts. `version-source.snapshot.json` records the published npm version observation. Fresh, question and later-recall NDJSON files contain selected native identity/assistant/result records, preserved byte for byte. These are excerpts, not complete native streams.

The four app-server request schemas were generated by this CLI, not hand-edited. Native model/list captures cover visible models and includeHidden results.

The live probes use synthetic data only. Old versioned fixtures remain intact.
